memory_update.text: ZBRA should remain the benchmark/reference name for AIDC hardware exposure, but it is less underfollowed than the desired discovery lane.
PI is a high-relevance mid-cap pure-play for RAIN RFID chips/readers/software and should be prioritized for deeper validation of retail category expansion and customer concentration.
BRC is a lower-attention identification/labeling candidate; AB&R acquisition may increase barcode/RFID implementation exposure, but retail-specific contribution needs verification.
SPSC is an adjacent compliance-middleware chokepoint rather than a tag/printer vendor; retailer mandate complexity may increase supplier reliance on its trading-partner network.

Avery Dennison is highly relevant for intelligent labels and Walmart RFID fresh-category work, but was excluded from the candidate list due to the four-name cap and because this pass emphasized underfollowed discovery names.

node: RFID, barcode, labeling, serialization, and retailer compliance infrastructure
summary: Expanded the universe around retailer-driven RFID, barcode, labeling, and compliance infrastructure. The stronger underfollowed lane is not the retailers themselves, but companies selling item-level identification chips/readers, thermal barcode/RFID hardware, label/tag consumables, specialty identification systems, and EDI/compliance middleware that suppliers need to satisfy large-retailer mandates. This pass favors mid-cap or lower-attention names with direct exposure to inventory accuracy, omnichannel visibility, supplier compliance, and retail trading-partner networks. No buy/sell view is implied.
